key_insight: A transverse-field Ising model with a global, non-monotonic time-dependent field can simulate arbitrary quantum circuits with only polynomial overhead, making it computationally equivalent to gate-model quantum computing in principle.
engineering_relevance: This gives a theoretical bridge between analog Ising-based hardware and universal quantum computation, while also implying limits on efficient classical simulation of such driven Ising systems.
method: Use a global transverse field on the Ising model with time-dependent control.
Construct a polynomial-overhead simulation of arbitrary quantum circuits.
Leverage a recent global-control result for Rydberg atoms as the foundation.
evidence_signal: The abstract states the authors provide a constructive proof with polynomial overhead in time, qubit number, and energy scale, rather than a numerical benchmark.
watch_item: The stated overheads are large, so the result is currently a proof of principle and not yet a practical recipe for near-term hardware.
paper_title: Polynomial equivalence of the global transverse-field Ising model and the gate model of quantum computation
